understanding how cells regulate the dynamic properties of their microtubules and how microtubules in turn influence the organization of the cell's cytoplasmic matrix.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between posttranslational microtubule modification and microtuble stability is cell type specific.
in human cells the stable microtubule population is the acetylated and/or detyrosinated subset of the microtubule network.
the posttranslational modifications of tubulin are not a prerequisite for the stability of microtubules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
posttranslational microtubule modification and microtudule stability are related but not synonymous phenomena.
microtubule dynamics are not only a function of microtubule polymerization but also of posttranslatalional modification and microtubuie stability.
the microtubule population is a dynamic equilibrium between the microtubules that have been modified and the microtubular population that is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microtubules of a cell are not a homogenous population.

posttranslational modifications and microtubules stability can be decoupled, and that microtubules with different posttranslational patterns can be stabilized or destabilized by modulating their rates of turnover.
posttranslational modifications of tubulin are not a simple on/off phenomenon.
